# Argo CD: Perpetual Drift Mechanics

Four distinct causes of perpetual `OutOfSync` state that are Argo CD/Helm/
Grafana controller behavior, not misconfiguration. Observed on a k3s cluster
running Argo CD with Sealed Secrets and kube-prometheus-stack, 2026-08.

## `ignoreDifferences` on core-API resources loses its `group` key

Argo CD's Application admission strips `group: ""` from
`spec.ignoreDifferences[]` entries that target core-API resources such as
`Service` and `Secret`. The source manifest has the key; the live
`Application` object does not. The carve-out entry itself then loops
`OutOfSync` — the diff-ignore rule that was supposed to suppress drift
becomes a source of drift. Omitting `group:` entirely for core-API resources
(and keeping it only for non-core API groups, where the admission does not
strip it) avoids the loop.

## `kubeseal` output always drifts on `creationTimestamp`

`kubeseal` emits `spec.template.metadata.creationTimestamp: null` in the
`SealedSecret` it generates. The Kubernetes API server strips null
timestamps on admission, so the live object never has the field — every
`SealedSecret` drifts on this json pointer until it's added to
`ignoreDifferences`. This is a universal quirk of `kubeseal`'s output shape,
not specific to any one secret or chart.

## `Synced` does not mean the live resource changed

Argo CD reports `Synced` once it has applied the rendered manifests — not
once the live resource's content has actually changed. If Helm renders
byte-identical output for a revision (e.g., a values edit that doesn't
affect the templated fields), the live resource's `resourceVersion` never
bumps. `Synced` after a values-file edit is easy to misread as "my edit
reached the cluster" when in fact the rendered output was unchanged and
nothing new was ever sent to the API server.

## Grafana datasource provisioning preserves stale UIDs by name match

Grafana's datasource provisioning matches existing datasources by **name**
at startup and preserves the existing datasource's `uid` across restarts. A
dashboard JSON that hard-codes a datasource UID resolves to whatever UID
that name currently has — which can be stale relative to what the
provisioning file now specifies. Forcing UID rotation requires a
`deleteDatasources` directive in the provisioning file to remove the
name-matched datasource before it's recreated with the new UID.

### Related chart-specific quirk: kube-prometheus-stack 84.5.0

kube-prometheus-stack 84.5.0 silently ignores `sidecar.datasources.uid` — the
auto-provisioned Prometheus datasource keeps its default `prometheus` UID
regardless of that value. The workaround observed: set
`defaultDatasourceEnabled: false` and add an explicit
`additionalDataSources` entry with the desired UID instead of relying on the
sidecar-generated one.
